column2: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

column1: # The NPDM declares 48 MiB of system resources. Startup requests a 6.20 GiB heap.
# The game steps its time by a frame ratio, its base rate / its frame rate, whatever the frame took: frames longer than a vsync played in slow motion. The ratio takes the host's
# frame step instead (MATCH_FRAME_STEP in patches.py, found by its function on any build that keeps it): 1 vsync at 60 fps, 2 when 60 does not hold, so game time = real time
# A late frame is shown late rather than held a second vsync (the game still steps by the vsyncs that passed, so its speed stays right): on a MacBook Air M4 the bridge in Kokiri
# Forest runs at about 52 fps this way (frame p50 19.5 ms), against a steady 30 with the hold; the launcher's Hold frames when late turns it back on
# agl wraps its depth clears in render conditions, as on Donkey Kong Bananza and Splatoon Raiders: in Kokiri Forest the main opaque pass tests EQUAL against a copy of the prepass depth
# that a conditional clear (skipped on the console) wiped first, so no lit geometry landed and the full-screen sky showed through everywhere (a white scene)

# The game turns the difference of two raw counter reports into its wind and particle time step at the Switch 2's system counter rate. At NVN's 614.4 MHz the step was 19.66 times too large: foliage, leaves and hanging plants moved about 20 times too fast (PR #1714; oot-mac7 keeps #1663's choice of no gpu_timestamps / draw_barriers keys)
# Terrain height tiles are filled by the CPU in mixed CPU/GPU pools without an NVN flush.
# Experimental high-rate support; default stays 60. See the game note for validation limits.

# The replay's Metal encoding on a thread of its own, as on iOS: the submit thread no longer waits for each pass's encoding, the GPU of a MacBook Air M4 starves less at segment boundaries (frame p50 24.5 → 23.5 ms at 1920x1080 docked, the Hyrule Field view)
# The game's compute dispatches with no barrier of its between them run side by side (nvn_mtl.m dispatch_enc): on the kokiri-deck route GPU p50 15.63 -> 14.76 ms (docked,
# Apple M4 Pro, three runs a side), the pictures alike
# The same event again: with the encode thread the replay still began translating at the signal. Translating the parked queue before it, its commits held until the signal, in
# Kakariko Village (headless, DM_FPS_HOLD=off, Apple M4 Pro, 2026-11-11): 55.5-57.1 -> 59.6-59.8 fps, frame p50 17.2-17.7 -> 16.5-16.6 ms, the GPU work and the draws the same
